text: Vietnam extends health insurance support for ethnic minorities

The government has issued Resolution No. 48/2026/NQ-CP extending health insurance premium subsidies for ethnic minority residents living in communes in Region II and Region III, as well as extremely disadvantaged villages in ethnic minority and mountainous areas during the 2016-2020 period that were no longer classified as disadvantaged in the 2021-2025 period.
Under the resolution, the state budget will continue covering at least 70 percent of health insurance premiums for eligible ethnic minority residents in these areas.

To implement the policy, the government tasked the Ministry of Finance with balancing and allocating central budget funds to support localities in accordance with the State Budget Law, while Vietnam Social Security (VSS) was instructed to guide provincial and municipal social security offices in executing the program.
Eligible beneficiaries who renew their participation within the prescribed timeframe will have their health insurance cards maintained continuously without interruption.
Provincial and municipal People's Committees are also directed to raise public awareness and compile and manage lists of eligible beneficiaries in their localities.
Resolution No. 48/2026/NQ-CP took effect on November 11, 2026.

For eligible patients admitted to medical facilities prior to November 11, 2026, whose treatment continues on or after that date, health insurance benefits will remain valid throughout their entire course of treatment.
Previously, under Decree No. 75/2023/ND-CP, the state budget funded at least 70 percent of health insurance premiums for this group over 36 months, from November 1, 2023, through October 31, 2026.

According to the Ministry of Health, three years of implementing Decree 75 helped maintain health insurance coverage for an average of roughly 2 million people annually, curbing drop-offs in participation after their communities no longer qualified for fully state-funded cards.
The Ministry of Health estimates that around 1.3 million ethnic minority residents will continue benefiting under Resolution No. 48/2026/NQ-CP.

The Ministry of Finance projects that the 70 percent state subsidy will require approximately VND207 billion ($8.15 million) in the final two months of 2026, with average annual funding estimated at over VND1.2 trillion ($47.24 million) during the 2027-2030 period.
